cards.text: This is the burden Habakkuk the prophet received in a vision. And it doesn't open with a polite little prayer, friend. Habakkuk opens by crying out to the LORD, and he's got QUESTIONS.

cards.question: Habakkuk's first words to the LORD are "How long". What does that tell you about his prayer?

answers.text: He has been calling for help a while
He is praying for the very first time
He wants to know how long the vision lasts

cards.question: True or false: Habakkuk says he cries out to the LORD, "Violence!" but the LORD does not save.

cards.text: Look what's in front of Habakkuk, friend: destruction and violence. Strife is ongoing, and conflict abounds.

cards.question: Habakkuk asks the LORD why He makes him see iniquity. He also asks why the LORD tolerates ___.

cards.text: Because of it all, Habakkuk says, the law is paralyzed and justice never goes forth.

cards.question: Habakkuk says justice is perverted. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The wicked hem in the righteous
The king has left the city

cards.text: Now the LORD answers: "Look at the nations and observe—be utterly astounded!" Not mildly surprised, not "huh, neat," but UTTERLY astounded.

cards.question: The LORD says He is doing a work in your days. How hard will it be to believe?

answers.text: You would never believe it even if told
Only the wise will understand it at first
Everyone will see it coming from far away

cards.text: So what's this unbelievable work? The LORD says He is raising up a nation.

cards.question: Which nation does the LORD say He is raising up?

cards.text: The Chaldeans, a people from Babylon (Jeremiah 50:1). The LORD calls them that ruthless and impetuous nation, and they march through the breadth of the earth.

cards.question: Why do the Chaldeans march through the breadth of the earth?

answers.text: To take homes that belong to others
To take back land they once owned
To hunt down one rival king

cards.text: Homes that aren't theirs, friend. The LORD says they are dreaded and feared.

cards.question: True or false: The Chaldeans get their idea of justice from themselves.

cards.text: Deciding their own justice, like writing your own performance review and naming yourself employee of the month. Then the LORD turns to their horses, comparing them to leopards and to wolves of the night.

cards.question: Leopards and wolves of the night. What do those pictures say about the Chaldeans' horses?

cards.text: Swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves, friend. Their horsemen charge ahead, and their cavalry comes from afar.

cards.question: The LORD says the Chaldeans fly like a vulture. What is that vulture doing?

cards.text: All of them come bent on violence, their hordes advancing like the east wind. That word again, friend: violence.

cards.question: As their hordes advance, the LORD says the Chaldeans gather ___ like sand.
The Chaldeans scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. True or false: A strong fortress makes them turn back.

cards.text: They LAUGH at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it. Then they sweep by like the wind and pass through.

cards.question: The LORD says the Chaldeans are guilty. Their own ___ is their god.

cards.text: We'll stop the oven timer right here for now. Stick with me, friend, because Habakkuk and the LORD are just getting started.
